To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a dicistronic retroviral vector containing a mutated DHFR gene is equally effective in conferring MTX resistance to mouse hematopoietic stem cells as a double copy vector.
the use of SFF-based dicistronic retroviral vectors will not improve gene transfer and transgene expression in hematopoietics cells compared with N2-based double-copy vectors.
the protection of hematopoeitic cells from methotraxate toxicity is the same for both the DC/SV and the SFG retroviral vectors, but that the SFG vectors confer higher protection to NIH3T31 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of retroviral vectors for gene therapy.
the comparison of the protection provided by methotrexate to NIH3T31 and hematopoietetic cells infected with retroviral vectors containing the SFG and DC/SV6 backbone.
the comparison of MTX protection of two different retrovirus vectors containing the S31 mutant DHFR cDNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SFG-based vector is not better than the DC/SV vector in terms of transgene expression in the hematopoietic cell line.
the DC/SV vector is a superior retroviral vector for the delivery of the S31 DHFR gene into hematopoietic stem cells.
the SFG and DC/SV6 vectors have equal efficiency for transgene expression in hematopoietically derived cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SFG vectors are more efficient for NIH3T3 cell gene transfer than DC/SV6 vectors, but that both vectors are equally efficient for gene transfer to hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.

the DC/SV vector is more efficient than the SFG vector for transduction of human hematopoietically derived cells, but the SFG vector has the advantage of higher expression of DHFR in NIH3T3 fibroblasts.
the use of a dicistronic retroviral vector for the transfer of the DHFR cDNA is not superior to a double copy vector for the protection of hematopoeitic progenitor cells from MTX toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the dicistronic SFG-based vector does not improve gene transfer over the double copy vector.
the SFG vector provides higher transgene expression than the DC/SV vector in NIH3T3 fibroblasts but not in hematopoietics cells.
the use of S31 DHFR-containing SFG-based retroviral vectors is not a viable option for protection of hematopoiesis from MTX toxicity.
